claims.text: A machine-learning model trained on high-entropy-alloy data can accurately identify alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The machine-learning model will outperform current thermal-conductivity predictions.
The target materials are high-entropy alloys in an unprocessed state.
The training dataset contains high-entropy alloys with known thermal-conductivity properties.
Composition, processing, and microstructure are relevant predictors of high-entropy-alloy properties.
A machine-learning model can identify patterns linking composition, processing, and properties.
Learning these patterns will improve thermal-conductivity prediction accuracy.
More accurate identification of low-phonon-thermal-conductivity alloys will enable optimized thermal-insulation properties.
Model performance is limited by training-data quality.
Model performance is limited by training-data quantity.
Model performance is limited by the complexity of composition-processing-property relationships.
The model may fail to generalize to unseen high-entropy alloys.
The model may overfit or underfit the training data.
Performance should be evaluated on a separate unseen dataset.
Predictive performance will be measured using mean absolute error and coefficient of determination.
Failure to perform significantly better than current predictions would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The target is described as unprocessed alloys, while processing is simultaneously presented as a key predictor and part of the predictive mechanism; the hypothesis does not explain how processing information applies to the stated unprocessed state.
